extracted.intended_audience: Team USA athletes and other accredited persons (athletes, team staff) engaging in social and digital media around the Olympic/Paralympic Games
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for athletes and accredited persons on permitted social and digital media activity during the Olympic and Paralympic Games, including commercial-use limits and audiovisual sharing restrictions. Covers timing (Games period), links to full IOC/IPC rules, and references to Rule 40 and Rule 50.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged social and digital media engagement (subject to conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IOC and IPC encourage athletes and other accredited persons to engage in social and digital media activities, sharing and celebrating their experiences with their global audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement is allowed and encouraged, but certain conditions apply (see commercial use and audio/video restrictions). Use the IOC/IPC resources (links and overview video) to understand specific limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial use restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some conditions apply regarding commercial use of social and digital media during the Games period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Athletes must comply with commercial guidelines and Rule 40; consult the IOC/IPC guidelines and USOPC commercial guidelines for specifics on what constitutes prohibited commercial activity during the Games.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio and video sharing restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions may apply to the sharing of audio and video content from the Games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because audio and video are specifically highlighted, athletes should review the IOC/IPC guidelines to determine permitted uses, rights, and any required permissions before posting game-related audiovisual material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: guidelines effective during Games times
rubrics_metrics.description: These guidelines apply during Games times. Both the IOC and IPC guidelines are in effect from the opening to the closing of the Olympic Villages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social and digital media conduct subject to these rules is evaluated only during the defined Games period (opening through closing of the Olympic Villages). Confirm exact dates for each Games edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 40 compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Athletes must be aware of and comply with Rule 40-related restrictions concerning athlete marketing and commercial activity during the Games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Rule 40 and related USOPC materials (links on the page) for details about permitted sponsor mentions, timing, and restrictions; Rule 40 background material is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: IOC Rule 50 awareness and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Athletes should be mindful of IOC Rule 50 (listed on the page) which contains rules relevant to athlete conduct during the Games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not detailed on this page, athletes must check IOC Rule 50 text (linked) for restrictions such as political demonstrations and other conduct rules during Olympic events and ceremonies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult official IOC and IPC guideline documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The full IOC guidelines and IPC guidelines are available via provided links and are the authoritative sources for specifics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the linked IOC and IPC pages for complete, up-to-date rules. The USOPC page is a summary; always verify details on the IOC/IPC websites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use provided overview resources (Paris 2024 video) and watch for updates
rubrics_metrics.description: An overview video on the Social Media Guidelines for Paris 2024 is available; Milano Cortina guidance was not yet available as of Fall 2025 but likely follows Paris principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch the overview video for a summary of key points and check IOC/IPC sites regularly for updates, especially for subsequent Games where guidelines may be revised.
